Saukenai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiauliai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. From 1867 to 1869, the rabbi of Saukenai was Yitzhak-Yaakov Reines, who later founded the Mizrachi party — the major organizational vehicle for Religious Zionism and one of the most influential streams within the broader Zionist movement, whose influence continues in Israeli religious politics today. The town's 18th-century wooden synagogue, famous for its carved bimah and Holy Ark, burned down in 1944. On July 31, 1941, 273 local Jews were murdered by a German Einsatzgruppen unit together with Lithuanian collaborators in a forest four miles north of town.
